test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements about the 2015 India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (LBA):

1) As per the 2015 agreement, 51 Bangladeshi enclaves in India and 111 Indian enclaves in Bangladesh were exchanged.

2) A majority of enclave residents from Bangladesh opted to retain Bangladeshi citizenship after the transfer.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 is Correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2015 Land Boundary Agreement (LBA)** was a historic treaty between **India** and **Bangladesh** that facilitated the transfer of **111 Indian enclaves** (adversely held territories) located in Bangladesh and **51 Bangladeshi enclaves** located in India. This exchange involved roughly **17,160 acres** of land transferred to Bangladesh and **7,110 acres** of land transferred to India. **Hence, statement 1 is correct.**
 
• Following the transfer of sovereignty on **July 31, 2015**, residents of the enclaves were granted the right to choose their citizenship. According to the joint survey conducted by both nations, the vast majority of the residents in the **51 Bangladeshi enclaves** within India opted for **Indian citizenship**. Conversely, the majority of residents in the **111 Indian enclaves** within Bangladesh chose to remain there and accept **Bangladeshi citizenship**. Only **979 individuals** from the Indian enclaves in Bangladesh opted to move to the Indian mainland to retain their original citizenship. **Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The exchange was operationalized through the **100th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2015** of the Indian Constitution, which amended the **First Schedule** to redefine the boundaries of **Assam**, **West Bengal**, **Meghalaya**, and **Tripura**.
 
 
• **Historical Context**: The issue of **Chhitmahals** (enclaves) originated from the flawed **Radcliffe Award** of **1947**. Previous attempts to resolve it included the **Nehru-Noon Agreement** of **1958** and the **Indira-Mujib Accord** of **1974**.
 
• **Humanitarian Impact**: Before the **2015 LBA**, enclave residents were effectively stateless, lacking access to basic services like **healthcare**, **education**, and **legal protection** because officials from their parent country could not reach them.
 
• **Border Demarcation**: Besides the enclaves, the agreement also settled **6.1 kilometers** of **un-demarcated border** and addressed the issue of **Adverse Possessions**.
